summary: Round 12, narrow re-check against the round-11 bytes (b3caa6f4). Still prose only: no production logic, no wire change, and nothing in this diff adds, moves or authorises an object-store request. I checked only the two cells named as changed and did not re-derive a decision or a counted fact. BOTH ROUND-11 MAJORS ARE DISCHARGED. (A) M5.45h's criterion 1 at backlog.md:69 now asserts the count as 'at most one fetchDirectory and at most one fetchRange invocation per (node, segment)', which is an equality per sample rather than a property of a function of K, and it is falsifiable at the one share the criterion names: a per-run implementation reports 64 fetchRange invocations and reds, a Set<String> collapse still reds via the invocations-not-urls clause, the (segmentKey, indexId) cache reports 2 fetchRange and reds, and M5.66's header-plus-slice shape greens at 1 and 1 with no edit to a landed assertion. The headline now reads 'ONE FETCH OPERATION -- the SHARING unit ... whose request SHAPE is settled below and is not necessarily a single request', so the top-to-bottom contradiction with the clause below is gone, and the decode half ('ALL K RUNS DECODE THEIR OWN RECORDS FROM IT') is untouched so the empty-array coalescer still reds. (B) The span/sum half-landing is closed by DELETION, not annotation: the later sentence at backlog.md:126 now reads 'by invariant (ii), which is the SPAN' and carries only the open-ended bytes=byteStart- survivor and the ~400 whole-object mandate, both of which are independent of the bound. Criterion 2 now holds exactly one byte bound. (C) The third site is genuinely fixed: M5.66's resolution paragraph describes M5.45h by the two named invocations rather than by 'constant in K'. EVERYTHING I PASSED AT ROUNDS 9-11 SURVIVES: the two-sided boundary pair, invariants (i)/(ii)/(iii), the K = 1 and K = 2 evidence cases with their extremes fixture, the same-K-different-run-sizes case for (iii), the symmetric round-trip predicate, the codec read-and-refuse arm with the GoldenSegmentV1Test route, 3b's extent disagreement, the count-every-request-at-the-seam clause, the withdrawn cross-AZ arm, and the M5.45g + M5.45h dependency with its verified ground -- all byte-identical in substance and each still reds its named mutation. ONE THING BLOCKS, and it is the fourth instance of the same shape inside the cell the fix just edited: the justification sentence for the retracted 'constant in K' wording survives at backlog.md:69 and asserts the equivalence the same cell measured to be false, 900 characters after refuting it. It is one deletion in a file this diff already stages.

findings.title: The constancy retraction half-landed: the cell now both refutes 'constant in K' with a measured counter-example and, 900 characters later, still asserts constant-in-K loses nothing -- the one sentence in the cell that states an EQUIVALENCE between the formulations states it for the one that was just withdrawn
findings.failure_scenario:
THE TWO SENTENCES ARE IN DIRECT CONTRADICTION AND ONLY ONE IS MARKED AS SUPERSEDED. The new clause says the constancy wording is WEAKER than the literal and gives the measurement that proves it: 'a cache keyed (segmentKey, indexId) reports 2 at K = 64, RED under the literal 1 and GREEN under one sample, and it is indices-per-node scaling'. The surviving sentence says the opposite as a flat claim -- constant-in-K kills EVERY mutation the literal killed -- and supports it with the single-sample inference ('a per-run implementation reports 64 or 128 at K = 64, not a constant') that the clause above it names as the inference one evaluation cannot make. It carries no 'an earlier draft said' marker, unlike every other retraction in this cell and unlike the sum clause the same commit deleted outright in M5.66.

WALK THE READER WHO ACTS ON IT. M5.45g and M5.62 land and M5.45h is taken. The operative clause is correct and an owner following it writes two assertions, so the direct damage is bounded -- but the sentence is the cell's own stated equivalence, and it is reached by two readers who matter. (i) The owner who writes the test and then justifies its FORM: the criterion names exactly one share, K = 64, four times and no other; an owner who reads 'constant-in-K kills every mutation the literal 1 killed' has the cell's written permission to express the count as constancy observed at that one share -- isEqualTo(observed), isLessThan(K), or a fetchRange-only count -- because the cell states it forfeits nothing. Under that form the (segmentKey, indexId) cache passes: one fetchRange per (node, segment, index), which at a node holding 400 runs across, say, 40 indices is 40 whole-object GETs against one 8 MiB object. That is indices-per-node scaling, forbidden by non-negotiable 6 by name, and the cell measured it as the exact cost of the wording it kept the justification for. (ii) The next editor of this cell, who finds a live sentence saying the withdrawn wording was equivalent and reverts the criterion to it on the cell's own authority -- the milestone's most repeated defect, which this row names twice, running in the opposite direction.

AND IT IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE SHAPE IN TWO CELLS. Round 11 blocked on the span/sum half-landing; this commit fixed that by deletion, fixed M5.66's stale description of M5.45h, and left the stale justification standing in the cell whose criterion the whole round was about. A correction applied to one of two places, inside the edit that was made to stop applying corrections to one of two places.

WHAT CLOSES IT: delete the clause '⚠️ CONSTANT-IN-K KILLS EVERY MUTATION THE LITERAL 1 KILLED: a per-run implementation reports 64 or 128 at K = 64, not a constant.' The mutation it names is already covered, and covered more exactly, by the surviving sentence 'Naming the two invocations keeps the exactness the literal had: it reds 2, 64 and 128 alike' -- so the deletion removes a false claim and loses no coverage. One sentence, no new obligation, in the file this diff already stages.
